exposure: Progression from mild to moderate HIE
cohort: The study included 366 (near)-term infants with mild hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) and normal amplitude-integrated electroencephalography background.
finding: Mild HIE infants who progressed to moderate HIE showed increased cerebral injury (cerebral metabolite perturbations and higher white matter injury scores) and a higher incidence of abnormal neurological outcomes, while therapeutic hypothermia did not significantly improve abnormal outcomes within the progressive group.
